skill.name: aws-serverless
skill.description: Guides building AWS Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, SQS/SNS, SAM, and CDK serverless applications with operational patterns.
skill.summary: Build and review AWS serverless applications with Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, SAM, and CDK patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, JavaScript template literals, AWS environment configuration, or AWS terminology. One network egress finding is confirmed because the sample allows HTTPS egress to 0.0.0.0/0, and semantic review found wildcard CORS and a destructive CDK removal policy as copy-paste risks.

remediation.issue: Broad outbound network egress is shown for a Lambda security group.
remediation.suggestion: Replace 0.0.0.0/0 with VPC endpoints, private network ranges, or controlled egress paths where possible.

remediation.issue: API examples use wildcard CORS origins, headers, or methods.
remediation.suggestion: Show production examples with explicit trusted origins, limited methods, and only required headers.

remediation.issue: The CDK DynamoDB example uses RemovalPolicy.DESTROY.
remediation.suggestion: Default production examples to RETAIN and place destructive policies only in clearly separated development snippets.

remediation.issue: Deployment commands can create AWS resources and costs.
remediation.suggestion: Add a reminder to review account, region, IAM role, and cost impact before running sam deploy or cdk deploy.

semantic_findings.title: Wildcard CORS Configuration in Production Examples
semantic_findings.description: The skill presents wildcard CORS settings in API Gateway and handler examples. Copying these into production can expose APIs to unintended browser origins.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly uses Access-Control-Allow-Origin *, AllowOrigins *, AllowHeaders *, and CDK ALL_ORIGINS or ALL_METHODS. The surrounding text claims production-ready guidance, so this is a realistic copy-paste risk.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive CDK Removal Policy in Main Example
semantic_findings.description: The CDK example sets a DynamoDB table removal policy to destroy. If copied into a production stack, deleting the stack can delete persistent application data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The line explicitly uses cdk.RemovalPolicy.DESTROY on a DynamoDB table. The inline comment says it is for development only, which lowers severity but does not remove copy-paste risk.

content.value_statement: Serverless teams need repeatable patterns for Lambda APIs, queues, streams, and storage. This skill provides AWS-focused templates, deployment guidance, and operational checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates Lambda handler patterns for Node.js and Python with API Gateway responses.
Provides SAM and CDK examples for Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, and SQS.
Explains SQS batch failure handling and DynamoDB Streams processing patterns.
Recommends cold start, timeout, memory, VPC, and payload size improvements.
Lists validation checks for credentials, IAM wildcards, DLQs, SDK usage, and table naming.
limitations: It does not deploy infrastructure or verify AWS account state by itself.
Examples require review for IAM, CORS, networking, cost, and compliance needs.
It focuses on AWS serverless services, not GCP or Azure serverless platforms.
It does not replace a security review for production workloads.

use_cases.title: Create a Lambda API
use_cases.description: Plan a Lambda-backed HTTP API with DynamoDB storage, handler structure, and local test events.

use_cases.title: Define Serverless Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Draft SAM or CDK resources for API Gateway, Lambda functions, queues, and DynamoDB tables.

use_cases.title: Review Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Check serverless designs for cold starts, timeouts, payload limits, retries, and runaway invocation risks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Lambda Handler
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single function pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Node.js Lambda handler for an API Gateway request. Include input parsing, error handling, and a DynamoDB read.

prompt_templates.title: Design an HTTP API
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for API and database infrastructure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a SAM template for a small HTTP API with Lambda and DynamoDB. Include least privilege policies and local test guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Event Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an event-driven AWS serverless pipeline using SQS, Lambda, and DynamoDB Streams. Include retries, DLQ handling, and idempotency notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of existing serverless code or infrastructure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SAM or CDK serverless design for production readiness. Focus on IAM, CORS, network egress, cold starts, timeout, memory, recursion, and cost risks.

output_examples.input: I need a CRUD API for items using Lambda and DynamoDB.
output_examples.output: A structured plan with Lambda handlers, API routes, DynamoDB table design, SAM resources, IAM policy scope, and local test steps.

output_examples.input: My SQS-triggered Lambda keeps retrying the whole batch.
output_examples.output: A diagnosis of batch failure behavior, a partial failure handling approach, DLQ settings, and idempotency checks.

output_examples.input: Review this CDK stack before production deployment.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review covering IAM scope, CORS, removal policies, timeouts, memory, VPC egress, alarms, and rollback risks.

best_practices: Scope IAM permissions, CORS origins, and network egress before production deployment.
Set explicit timeouts, memory, DLQs, alarms, and concurrency limits for critical functions.
Test locally, review generated infrastructure, and deploy only after confirming account-specific settings.
anti_patterns: Copying sample wildcard CORS or open egress settings directly into production.
Deploying Lambda functions without cost controls, retry limits, or dead letter handling.
Using one generic serverless pattern for workloads with different latency, data, or compliance needs.

faq.question: Can this skill deploy AWS infrastructure?
faq.answer: It provides commands and templates, but deployments require user approval, AWS credentials, and account-specific review.

faq.question: Which AWS services does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, DynamoDB Streams, S3, SAM, CDK, and CloudWatch patterns.

faq.question: Does it support both SAM and CDK?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes SAM templates, CDK stack examples, local development commands, and deployment guidance.

faq.question: Is the output production ready?
faq.answer: The patterns target production concerns, but every example needs review for IAM, CORS, data retention, cost, and compliance.

faq.question: Does it require AWS credentials?
faq.answer: Reading and adapting the guidance does not require credentials. Running deploy commands or account checks requires AWS credentials.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that need AWS serverless guidance.
